reason: Backfill is_package/itinerary_nights (schema v4) and reclassify NCL SOLO_GUEST_ONLY from availability_status=limited to solo_only. Two defects found 2026-09-15: (1) NCL land+cruise cruisetours were stored unmarked, so price_pppn divided a package fare by cruise-segment nights and read ~2x the true nightly cruise rate; (2) Studio single-occupancy cabins were counted as scarcity, putting 43% of NCL Caribbean inside cells in a depletion bucket containing no depletion. availability_status was re-derived from availability_status_raw, preserved in the original rows. is_package came from scripts/probe_sail_dates.py querying NCL's sailings endpoint on 2026-09-15/16 -- it is a stable product attribute, NOT something observed in the original scrape. No price, sailing, cabin or scrape_ts value was altered; row counts and natural keys are unchanged.

Re-collected 2026-09-16 under a widened weekly-full scope (step 3). Three scope changes applied since this day's first run: (1) sail_window start moved 2027-01-01 -> 2026-10-01, so near-term sailings now enter weekly-full; (2) Carnival dest sweep ['E','C','BH','BM','A'] replaced by an unfiltered sweep, which reached 482 itinerary records instead of 402; (3) Carnival regionCode ET->Transatlantic and CP->Caribbean added, and the embark-port fallback restricted to itineraries with no regionCode. Net effect on this file: +1240 rows. NOT purely a scope change: 12 cells also moved price (price_total/price_pppn/price_per_person, with rate_code/offer_id shifts) between the 04:00 and 08:00 UTC runs -- genuine intraday repricing by Carnival, captured here because the whole day was re-collected. scrape_ts_utc and raw_response_path changed on all rows because these are new fetches, not a reprocessing of the earlier payloads.

Deleted 2026-09-16__weekly-full__norwegian-cruise-line.jsonl.gz and purged 4,470 NCL rows at market=CA / currency=CAD. Cause: the step-3 widened-window collection was run from a local machine with Canadian egress. NCL resolves market from client IP at the Akamai edge, so every NCL row came back in CAD. Nothing refused them: market_for() recorded the served market faithfully but no guard rejected it, so the rows were written and exported. Carnival was unaffected -- its search takes an explicit currency=USD parameter and already asserted USD per row. Fix shipped alongside this purge: parse_sailings now raises CurrencyMismatch on any priced row that is not EXPECTED_CURRENCY=USD, and NCLSource.collect stops the line on that error and records it as fatal, so a non-US egress fails the run instead of filling the panel. NCL for 2026-09-16 must be re-collected on a US-hosted runner.
